Starting from the United States Grand Prix weekend on Friday, October 23, Apple TV will offer Formula 1 broadcasts featuring Dolby Atmos technology on supported devices. Here are the details.

"Combining outstanding picture quality with exceptional sound to fully capture the thrilling passion of this sport"

Apple and Dolby Laboratories have announced a new collaboration to introduce Dolby Atmos technology to Formula 1 live broadcasts on Apple TV, beginning with the United States Grand Prix weekend in Austin, Texas on October 23.

Apple stated that Dolby Atmos, working together with Dolby Vision, will "deliver a more immersive viewing experience," making "fans feel as though they are at the heart of the action, completely surrounded by the energy, drama, and emotion of Formula 1."

Below is the response from Oliver Schusser, Apple's Vice President of Music and International Content, regarding this announcement:

It is worth noting that Apple's Formula 1 streaming rights are currently limited to the United States only, with no additional subscription required—viewers only need an Apple TV subscription to watch.

Apple previously offered free streaming of the Bahrain Grand Prix in the United States, and also partnered with Netflix to bring Season 8 of "Formula 1: Drive to Survive" to Apple TV in the United States. As part of the same collaboration, the 2026 Canadian Grand Prix will also be live-streamed on both Apple TV and Netflix in the United States.

Apple acquired the U.S. streaming rights to Formula 1 in 2025, with this five-year agreement taking effect from the 2026 season. Apple has previously stated its intention to expand its F1 race broadcasts to more regional markets.

Apple's broader partnership with Formula 1 also includes the film "F1: The Movie," which earlier this year won the Academy Award for Best Sound, and remains Apple's most successful theatrical release to date.

Apple TV's monthly subscription is US$14.99, or available through the Apple One bundle. The platform features numerous popular TV shows and films, including "Ted Lasso," "Severance," "The Studio," "The Morning Show," "Shrinking," and "Silo."
